correctness.rationale: From row-stochastic P^2=J and PJ=J it follows JP=J, so P is doubly stochastic. A deterministic row leads to a uniform row at its target but that contradicts the target column sum, including the self-loop case. Thus all rows have support at least 2; in n<=3 every pair overlaps, giving Dobrushin delta(P)<1. Compactness of the exact-square kernel set yields a uniform max rho_n<1; successive Dobrushin contractions cover every arbitrary switching sequence, law and time. For n=4 forward/reverse two-bit shifts P,Q=P^T satisfy P^2=Q^2=J, but PQ is a nonuniform idempotent preserving a bit. Blending with J by epsilon preserves exact squares; (P_e Q_e)^m=J+(1-e)^(2m)(PQ-J) and corresponding odd products. Rows are supported equally on two states, giving exactly TV=(1-e)^t/2 and maximal relative error=(1-e)^t, including endpoints and both phases. Independent 120 rational checks reproduce these formulas; all-real proof is analytic.
